title: Penne con Melanzane
subtitle: Penne with roasted aubergine in a rich tomato sauce
excerpt: Penne con melanzane is aubergine and tomato sauce over penne: the Sicilian combination of aubergine fried or roasted until soft, then cooked into a tomato sauce that takes on the aubergine's richness. It is a substantial vegetarian pasta that needs no meat to feel complete.
sourceNotes: Pasta with aubergine is a classic of Sicilian and southern Italian cooking. Related to the famous pasta alla norma (with ricotta salata), this version omits the salted cheese for a simpler weeknight approach. Aubergine in tomato sauce is documented throughout southern Italian regional cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The aubergine sauce can be made 2 days ahead. Reheat with a splash of water and toss with freshly cooked penne.

content.text: Penne con melanzane is the straightforward version of the Sicilian aubergine-and-tomato pasta, without the ricotta salata that makes it alla norma. The aubergine is roasted rather than fried to keep it simpler, then cooked into the tomato sauce so it becomes almost part of the base. The result is a rich, satisfying pasta that eats like a meat sauce without any.

items.prepNote: about 600 g total, cut into 2 cm cubes
2 x 400 g tins, or 600 g fresh ripe tomatoes

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Toss the aubergine cubes with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil, a generous pinch of salt, and chilli flakes if using. Spread on a baking tray in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and soft. The cubes need colour to have flavour.

Warm the remaining olive oil in a wide pan. Cook the garlic gently for 2 minutes until pale gold. Add the tomatoes and crush with a spoon. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until slightly thickened. Add the roasted aubergine and cook together for 5 minutes. Stir in most of the basil. Taste and season.

Cook the penne in generously salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain. Add the penne to the sauce with a splash of pasta water and toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes. Scatter with remaining basil and pecorino to serve.

items.symptom: Aubergine is pale and spongy after roasting
items.cause: Tray was overcrowded, causing the aubergine to steam rather than roast
items.fix: Use two baking trays if needed and leave space between cubes. Aubergine needs direct oven heat to colour properly.

items.cause: Tomatoes were not reduced long enough
items.fix: Simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens noticeably, about 15 to 20 minutes. The aubergine adds body but only after the tomato base has concentrated.

items.symptom: Pasta sticks together in the sauce
items.cause: Pasta water was not added when tossing
items.fix: Always add a splash of the starchy pasta water when combining. It lubricates and helps the sauce cling to the pasta.

content.text: Aubergine with tomatoes is the key vegetable pairing in Sicilian and southern Italian cooking. Pasta alla norma: the Catanian version with ricotta salata and fried aubergine: is the most famous form. The simpler penne con melanzane is what most Sicilian households make in summer. The sauce also works as a pizza topping or bruschetta base, and is good cold the next day.
